records.name: Art City Opera
records.summary: A Philadelphia opera company that stages full productions, many exploring current social issues, and runs workshops for early-career singers.
records.what_you_do: Attend a production (tickets go through the company's ticketing link), watch the newsletter for audition postings, and join a workshop for early-career singers when one is offered.

schedule.text: Productions for the 2026 to 2027 season are listed on the site, but no performance dates are shown yet.

cost.text: Ticket prices and any workshop fees are not shown. Donations are accepted.

first_step.how: Buy a ticket to a production through the ticketing link on artcityopera.org, or sign up for the newsletter to hear about auditions and workshops.
first_step.basis: Anyone can attend a production, but performing needs an audition and the page does not explain how to start.

records.notes: The batch liveness check lists 2026-08 as the newest date, but no August 2026 date appears on the page read here, so that date is not used. The batch's IRS address (1500 Chestnut St, Suite 2) is not confirmed as a venue, so no location is recorded. The page shows no volunteer roles, membership, or classes; the workshops are mentioned without details. Status is probably_active because the site is current (2026 to 2027 season) but shows no dated items.

records.name: Asylum Pride House
records.summary: Helps LGBTQIA+ asylum seekers and immigrants with transitional housing, case help, legal support, and donated supplies. Volunteers and supporters can take part through volunteer calls, events, and trainings.
records.what_you_do: Join the email list for volunteer calls, donate supplies through the group's registry, or come to a public event such as the Welcome Walk. Groups can also ask for a speaker or a tabling event.

schedule.text: Welcome Walk on Saturday, October 24, 9 to 11 am at the Ott Center. Rainbow Ribbons holiday gift drive in November, date to be announced.

cost.text: Transitional housing is described as no cost. Fees for events and trainings are not listed. Donations are welcome.

first_step.how: Join the email list on asylumpridehouse.org for volunteer calls, or register for the Welcome Walk through the link on the site.
first_step.basis: The site has a clear public way in through an email list and public events, and no application is described for volunteers.

records.notes: The Welcome Walk is listed as Saturday, October 24 with no year. October 24 is a Saturday in 2026, and the group was founded in 2022, so it is recorded as October 2026. The Rainbow Ribbons drive has no date yet. The support request runs through a form on the site; no form was filled in. Mailing address only, so it is not recorded as a walk-in site.

records.name: Atlantic Center for Capital Representation
records.summary: A Philadelphia legal group that fights death sentences and other extreme punishments. It represents people directly, brings test cases, and trains lawyers on the same work.
records.what_you_do: Use the volunteer sign-up form on the site to offer help; the page does not describe the roles. Training is offered with a registration link, and donations are accepted.

cost.text: No fees for training or events are listed on the page.

first_step.how: Fill in the volunteer sign-up form linked from atlanticcenter.org. The page does not say what a first task looks like.
first_step.basis: The site has a clear public volunteer sign-up, and no application is described.

records.notes: The site names a 2026 Fall Gala with no date, place, or time. Training is listed with a register link but no dates or price. No dated news items were found, so status is probably_active rather than active. The only public way in is the volunteer form.

records.name: Autistic Art Coalition of Philadelphia
records.summary: An autistic-led group that runs free art classes, exhibitions, and community events for autistic, neurodivergent, and disabled artists in the Delaware Valley.
records.what_you_do: Take a free art class, show work at an exhibition, or come to a community event such as the Community Paint Day or The Infinity Ball. Ask about volunteer roles through the mailing list.

schedule.text: Published hours: Monday noon to 5 pm, Tuesday 3:30 to 8 pm, Thursday 11 am to 5 pm, Friday noon to 5 pm, Saturday by appointment. Express Yourself meets Thursdays 1 to 2:30 pm, run with Liberty Resources; its meeting place is not published.

cost.text: Classes are free for eligible artists in the Delaware Valley. Donations are accepted. Infinity Ball ticket prices are not shown.

first_step.how: Join the mailing list on aacophilly.org, or call the hotline at 215-934-2116 to ask about the next free class.
first_step.basis: The page says no experience is needed for the free classes and gives a mailing list and a phone line to start.

records.notes: Legal name Autistic Art Coalition of Philadelphia (AACOP). Per the page, free classes are for autistic, neurodivergent, intellectually disabled, and disabled artists in the region. The Express Yourself meeting place is not published. Volunteer opportunities are mentioned without sign-up details. The batch liveness check shows 2026-10, which matches the page. Liberty Resources is named as the partner for Express Yourself; see leads_only.

records.name: Bar Association of the Third Federal Circuit
records.summary: A membership group for lawyers and court staff who practice before the federal appeals court for the Third Circuit. It runs appellate programs and receptions, and publishes a newsletter and a practice guide.
records.what_you_do: Members can take part in appellate programs, webinars, and bench and bar receptions. The association publishes a newsletter. The page does not say whether non-members can attend programs.

schedule.text: Programs are announced one at a time, in cities across the circuit including Philadelphia. No regular meeting day is published.

cost.text: Dues and program fees are not shown on the page.

first_step.how: Check the eligibility rules on the membership page at thirdcircuitbar.org, then join or renew online.
first_step.basis: Membership is limited to attorneys in good standing and court staff, and dues are not shown on the page.

records.notes: The newest item is a Court notice about a judgeship vacancy, dated 2026-03-19. The newest program the association itself lists is dated 2025-12-02, in Pittsburgh. The 2020 Judicial Conference is listed with a 2023 date, an inconsistency on the page. Membership is for lawyers, judges, and court staff, so this is not an open public group.
